#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This PR updates the comments about NetworkPolicySpec to more clearly indicate how its PolicyTypes field interacts with its PodSelector, Ingress, and Egress field.  Previously the comments on the other fields did not mention the critical role that PolicyTypes plays in their own meaning.

> Our API godocs should ALWAYS clearly define the semantics of the API. "Read the docs" should be for examples, advanced use cases. Put simply, if a user can't understand what the API does from this godoc, we either need to add more, or clarify more. Any important implication should be captured in the API.

The problem, as seen in this PR, is that the behavior of the API may depend on the interactions of multiple fields in the object, and so if you want to document all of the relevant behavior in the API docs, you have to put random bits of it into the documentations of fields that are only peripherally related.

This PR makes the API documentation more comprehensive, but I don't feel like it makes it _better_. We need to be able to include documentation for `networkingv1.NetworkPolicy` _as a whole_, and our documentation system does not let us do that.

@danwinship : I agree with your systemic critique in the broad sense, but in this particular case it is not so bad; the interactions are all among fields within one struct.  The currently merged comments really are inadequate.  Could you approve merging this PR and revisiting once there is a way for API comments to refer to whole-feature doc?

Well, I can't approve it anyway because you need an API approver. (By the same token, my "systemic critique" carries no official weight and does not prevent anyone else from approving it.)

I will say that all of the statements in your new comments are true.

> The problem, as seen in this PR, is that the behavior of the API may depend on the interactions of multiple fields in the object

I agreed with this at the beginning of the large paragraph, but by the time I got to the end I think the text won me over as an improvement.

I think it's OK to have multiple paths to understanding, reading each field isn't ideal if you want to understand in the abstract, but it's great if you only want to understand one field that it at least tells you the other fields it interacts with.

/approve

issue_context.title: NetworkPolicySpec field doc is outdated
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

I tried to understand exactly what NetworkPolicy objects mean, and got lost/confused.  https://groups.google.com/g/kubernetes-sig-network/c/6k1A8l5uxLY

For example, the comments on the `PolicyTypes` field does not precisely specify semantics, and the comments on the `Ingress` and `Egress` fields omit the significance of the `PolicyTypes` field.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected to find clear answers.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Try to figure out from the comments in `types.go` exactly how the `PolicyType` field of a `NetworkPolicySpec` interacts with the `Ingress` and `Egress` fields.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

<details>

review_comments:
Rather than mention policyTypes throughout, it might be simpler to phrase it something like this:

> Ingress is used only for policies whose policyTypes includes `Ingress`. For policies that do not have Ingress specified in their policyTypes, this field has no effect.
> List of ingress rules to be applied to the selected pods. If this field is empty then this network policy does not add any allowed ingress and serves solely to ensure that the pods it selects are isolated for ingress by default.
